sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: resolving a manager's direct reports; deleted_at: soft-delete filtering on active employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type; is_active: selecting active policies for entitlement resolution

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: listing an employee's requests; status: filtering by approval state (manager queue); leave_type_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for overlap/balance checks

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: fetching an employee's balances; policy_id: fetching balances per policy; fiscal_year: scoping balances to a fiscal year; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique balance row per employee/policy/year

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: listing a recipient's notifications; status: filtering unread/pending notifications; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: resolving notifications for a leave request

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail for a specific entity; performed_at: time-ordered audit queries; performed_by: audit trail by actor
data_notes: Six conceptual tables defined once and referenced by name: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, notifications, audit_logs. All repository interfaces have concrete pg-Pool-backed implementations. AuditLog/AuditRecord from DOMAIN.md are consolidated into a single audit_logs table (AuditRecord is the snake_case wire form of AuditLog; AuditServiceInterface is a service contract, not a persisted entity). LeaveStatus/LeaveType enum naming remains open (DOMAIN.md vs ARCHITECTURE.md divergence).

open_questions.question: Which naming scheme is canonical for LeaveStatus and LeaveType enums: DOMAIN.md (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity) or root ARCHITECTURE.md (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; ANNUAL/SICK/MATERNITY/PATERNITY/UNPAID/OTHER)?
open_questions.impact: Determines the persisted string values in leave_requests.status and leave_policies.leave_type, and the TypeScript enum definitions shared across model/repository/service layers. A wrong choice forces a data migration and breaks cross-module contracts.
candidate_options: Adopt DOMAIN.md scheme (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/...; lowercase leave types) as canonical
Adopt ARCHITECTURE.md scheme (PENDING/...; UPPERCASE leave types) as canonical
Reconcile: use DOMAIN.md statuses but ARCHITECTURE.md leave types

open_questions.question: Should the persistence layer define the missing IUnitOfWork concrete implementation (PgUnitOfWork) and the shared base repository / error types, given none exist in the codebase?
open_questions.impact: The transactionContract for approve/reject (status change + balance update + audit + notification) requires a concrete IUnitOfWork.withTransaction implementation and shared error types; without them the atomic write path cannot be implemented.
candidate_options: Create PgUnitOfWork + base repository + error types in this persistence slice
Defer to a separate shared-infrastructure phase and reference by interface only

open_questions.question: What migration mechanism should be established, given no migrations or knexfile currently exist?
open_questions.impact: The conceptual table specs must be turned into actual PostgreSQL tables; without a migration mechanism the code agent has no established path to generate and apply schema changes.
candidate_options: Adopt knex migrations (knex is already in package.json)
Adopt a plain SQL migration runner (node-pg-migrate or custom)
Adopt raw SQL files applied manually

transaction_contract: Approve/reject is a multi-step atomic write: update leave_requests.status + approved_by/approved_at, decrement leave_balances.used_days/remaining_days, insert an audit_logs row, and insert a notifications row. The service owns the unit of work. Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction take an optional PoolClient as the last parameter (defaulting to the shared pool when omitted). The service acquires a client from the pool, issues BEGIN, passes the client to each participating repository call, then COMMITs or ROLLBACKs. BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are issued only by the IUnitOfWork.withTransaction implementation (PgUnitOfWork), never by repositories. Read-only and single-write operations (create draft, cancel, list, balance read) do not require a transaction.
